subject: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?

messages.author: ccdb8f812f9911a1
messages.subject: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?
parts:
Hello All,

I am doing research on a burrowing mammal (bilby) and have a question for the secr community.

I have limited trapping data for one of the populations I am studying, but I do have data on their diurnal burrow locations (from radio-tracking) for a more substantial period of time. Burrow sharing is not uncommon in bilbies, particularly between female and young at foot.

My question is, would it violate secr assumptions to use these diurnal burrow locations as 'traps' in secr ('single' traps capturing only the radio-tagged individual each time)? 

I can appreciate this may be a stretch and not the typical input for secr, but I am keen to be able to estimate the density of this population despite the limited trapping data. Any suggestions are welcomed. 

Thanks, 
Cass

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?
parts:
Hello Cass
Here's my take, with the usual caveats that I don't have the full picture and others may disagree:
Your burrow data are really just a subsample of the telemetry locations of tagged individuals (assuming you didn't actually monitor burrows per se to see who used them at other times). That means the telemetry data have the strengths and peculiarities of  telemetry data in general: the estimate of scale from telemetry data may or may not match the scale of detection in traps, the relation between the telemetry sample and the trapped sample needs to be defined (see e.g.  Fig. 2 in https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-telemetry.pdf), and generally telemetry does not add much to SECR estimates of density. Estimation of density requires sampling the untagged animals, that by definition do not appear in the telemetry sample.
Murray

messages.author: ccdb8f812f9911a1
messages.subject: Re: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?
parts:
Thanks for your reply Murray, just to confirm, you are suggesting the burrow locations from radiotracking are best used as telemetry data rather than treating them as a 'trapped' individual (in the absence of a large trapping data set)?

I do have some trapping data for a small number of traps (~25-30 traps, used several times each over a 2 week period) in which I captured both 'tagged' and 'untagged' animals. I have combined this with telemetry data from the tagged animals (ie concurrent telemetry data, 21 nights of tracking, 1 fix per night). I have thought this dataset may be too small to produce reliable results in secr, but I would appreciate thoughts on this.

Thanks, 
Cass
